title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: people data with source-system access controls
summary: Hold: the briefing's statement that no ingestion cap is documented overlooks the connection and tenant quotas documented for the Graph connections it uses. It also treats the Permissions view as unconfirmed for people connectors even though the cited guidance covers each Copilot connector, and extrapolates future storage behaviour beyond the published plan.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to import external people data together with associated access control lists.
claims.quote: This release enables organizations to bring people data from external systems into Microsoft 365 along with associated access control lists (ACLs)

claims.claim: The planned imported people data can be scoped to specific individuals and groups.
claims.quote: The imported data can be scoped to specific individuals and groups

claims.claim: The planned capability lets Copilot reason over people data while respecting source-system permissions.
claims.quote: ensuring Copilot respects existing permissions defined in source systems.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Today's documented people connector data is visible to all users in the tenant by default.
claims.quote: By default, people data provided via a Copilot connector is visible to all users in the tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The current build guide requires everyone access on ingested item ACLs.
claims.quote: You must set the access control list (ACL) on items ingested by the connector to grant access to everyone.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The people connector pages do not document differentiated access, and no Learn page for the planned feature was found.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors differentiated access control ACL individuals groups default migration rollout 561326. Opened graph/peopleconnectors and microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/build-connectors-with-people-data; both describe everyone visibility.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Custom people connectors are built using Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.
claims.quote: You build Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data in the same way that you build other Copilot connectors, by using the Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.

claims.claim: A people connection must set contentCategory to people.
claims.quote: Copilot connectors that contain people data must have the value `people` in the `contentCategory` property of the `externalConnections` API.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Current people connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.
claims.quote: This connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Uploaded people data attributes are stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: When you upload people data, each user's data attributes are scoped to their Microsoft 365 user profile and stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the new differentiated-access control's default state.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors differentiated access control ACL individuals groups default migration rollout 561326. Read roadmap description and opened graph/peopleconnectors and build-connectors-with-people-data; no arrival default for the new control.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Migration of existing everyone-ACL people connections, including whether they change automatically, is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors differentiated access control ACL individuals groups default migration rollout 561326. Opened graph/peopleconnectors, build-connectors-with-people-data and connectors/manage-access-permissions; no people ACL migration procedure.

claims.claim: No admin UI, PowerShell cmdlet or API is documented for the planned differentiated scoping of people connector data.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors ACL information barriers profile cards Org Explorer migration default PowerShell permissions individuals groups. Opened peopleconnectors, build-connectors-with-people-data and Graph externalConnection v1.0/beta; people items still require everyone ACLs.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: General connector access permissions cannot currently be updated after connection creation.
claims.quote: Updating access permissions after you create the connection isn't currently supported.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The general permissions guidance describes deleting and recreating a connection whose configured visibility does not match the intended model.
claims.quote: In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection. Recreate the connection using the Custom setup flow and explicitly configure access permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, second bullet
claims.claim: Future ACL-scoped people data would still sit with the Microsoft 365 profile.
claims.quote: Searched: "people data" "scoped" "profile" "ACL". Opened peopleconnectors and build-connectors-with-people-data; storage is described for today's everyone-visible data, not for the planned differentiated-access design.
claims.fix: Remove 'so scoped data would still sit with the profile,' and retain the current-storage fact followed by 'How scoping applies to profile cards, Org Explorer and search is not yet documented.'

claims.claim: People connectors respect Microsoft Purview Information Barriers.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data comply with information barriers (IB) to ensure compliance across various platforms.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: How the new ACL scoping interacts with Information Barriers and non-Copilot people experiences is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors ACL information barriers profile cards Org Explorer migration default PowerShell permissions individuals groups; "people data" "scoped" "profile" "ACL". Opened peopleconnectors and build-connectors-with-people-data; no new ACL interaction described.

claims.claim: Nonmatched user identifiers are ignored, so mismatched source identifiers can cause people data to be omitted.
claims.quote: Nonmatched user accounts (`userPrincipalName` or `externalDirectoryObjectId`) are ignored.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Microsoft Graph ignores accounts without an Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph ignores accounts without an Exchange Online mailbox.

claims.claim: The supplied feature sources describe ingestion and grounding rather than a change introducing write actions.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors differentiated access control ACL individuals groups default migration rollout 561326. Read roadmap description, peopleconnectors and build-connectors-with-people-data; these describe ingestion and reasoning, not new source-system write actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: People data connections do not support staged connections.
claims.quote: Connections with people data don't support staged connections.

claims.claim: Microsoft separately advises piloting people connectors with a limited audience.
claims.quote: Before rollout, confirm governance, privacy, and admin requirements for your connector and pilot with a limited audience.

claims.claim: Connector-ingested people properties are read-only to users.
claims.quote: All properties ingested via the people connectors are read-only.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends disabling user editing of overlapping properties to avoid edits not appearing on profile cards.
claims.quote: We recommend that you disable user editing of any properties that are also ingested via people connectors to avoid scenarios where user edits aren't displayed on the profile card due to the precedence model.

claims.claim: No people-data-ingestion-specific meter or credit rate was found.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors licensing pricing ingestion meter quota limits Microsoft 365; "people" "connectors" "licensing" "ACL". Opened peopleconnectors, build-connectors-with-people-data and connectors/prerequisites; no people-ingestion meter or credit rate.

claims.claim: No cap is documented for people data ingestion.
claims.quote: If you reach the maximum limit of a single connection or the tenant level quota across all connections, you can't add more items until you exit the state.
claims.fix: Replace 'No meter, credit rate or cap is documented for people data ingestion at the time of writing' with 'No meter, credit rate or spending cap specific to the planned ACL capability was found at the time of writing.' This removes the broader ingestion-limit absence claim; the Graph connections documentation describes connection and tenant item quotas.

claims.claim: People data persists while the user is active and has a valid Microsoft 365 licence, subject to deletion.
claims.quote: People data is stored as long as the end user is active and has a valid Microsoft 365 license, provided no deletion request was made by the admin.

claims.claim: The people connectors page names Global Administrator and Copilot Administrator roles for configuration.
claims.quote: Only users with Global Administrator and Copilot Administrator roles can configure people connectors.

claims.claim: The general connector management page requires an AI administrator, differing from the role wording on the people connectors page.
claims.quote: To access and manage your Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator for your organization.

claims.claim: OAuth 2.0 authentication is required to set up people connectors.
claims.quote: To set up people connectors, OAuth 2.0 authentication is required.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The general Permissions view is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Permissions.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connector you want to review to open the details pane. Under Permissions, you can view the permissions set for the connector.

claims.claim: No API equivalent of the connection-level Permissions model view is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph externalConnection Permissions view API permission model everyone source ACL configuration. Opened manage-access-permissions and externalConnection resource v1.0/beta; no equivalent connection Permissions model property. Item ACL APIs are a different surface.

claims.claim: The partner-connector Copilot Visibility toggle is at Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connection > Copilot Visibility and controls inclusion in Copilot Search and Chat.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connection that you want to modify. Under Copilot Visibility, select the toggle to turn the connector on or off, and choose Save.

claims.claim: No documented API equivalent of the Copilot Visibility toggle was found.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "Copilot Visibility" API beta. Opened manage-connector, externalConnection v1.0/beta and connecting-external-content-manage-connections; enabledContentExperiences documents search, not equivalence to the Copilot Search/Chat toggle.

claims.claim: An admin UI for creating custom people data connections is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: custom people data connector create connection Microsoft 365 admin center user interface. Opened peopleconnectors and build-connectors-with-people-data; the custom route uses Graph. Search results describe prebuilt deployment and custom federated setup, not custom people ingestion UI.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections creates the connection, with people content categorisation required for people data.
claims.quote: Create a new externalConnection object. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections

claims.claim: A people connector can be deleted in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Delete.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center and navigate to the connectors section. On the Your Connections tab, select the connector you want to delete. Select the Delete option.

claims.claim: DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/{connectionId} deletes an external connection.
claims.quote: Deletes an externalConnection object. DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosohr

claims.claim: Deleting a people connector removes it from all instances, but delays can occur.
claims.quote: If a connector is deleted, it's removed from all instances, but delays can be expected.

claims.claim: Learn does not confirm that the Permissions view covers people connectors.
claims.quote: You can review and validate access permissions for each Microsoft 365 Copilot connector from the connection details pane in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.fix: Replace the Permissions-specific applicability disclaimer in controls[1].note and Governance controls with 'The Permissions view is documented for each Microsoft 365 Copilot connector; this does not document configuration of the planned differentiated people ACLs.' Retain the separate qualification on Copilot Visibility, which is documented for partner connectors.

claims.claim: The Copilot Visibility documentation describes partner connectors without confirming coverage of people connectors.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph connector Permissions Copilot Visibility toggle API externalConnection enabledContentExperiences access permissions update. Opened manage-connector and peopleconnectors; the visibility section specifies partner connectors and gives no people-connector applicability statement.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: Existing connectors can be reviewed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 Admin Center, go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections.
